title: CertBound Project Simulation Schema
description: Schema for an interactive, branching, stateful exam simulation used across all CertBound certification tracks (BA-201, PMP, AWS, CompTIA, etc.). One file = one full simulation.

simulationId.description: Unique slug for this simulation, used in URLs and DB keys.

title.description: Display title shown to the candidate.

version.description: Semantic version of this simulation content, for tracking edits.

description.description: One-paragraph candidate-facing summary shown on the simulation's landing/intro card.

estimatedMinutes.description: Rough completion time shown to the candidate before starting.

domains.description: Ordered list of certification domains this simulation walks through. Used to render a progress rail in the UI.

initialState.description: Starting values for all numeric state variables tracked through the simulation. Add/remove keys as needed per simulation — the engine should treat this object as the source of truth for which state variables exist.

scenes.description: All scenes in the simulation, spine and detours combined, as a flat array. Order in the array does NOT determine play order — `nextScene` pointers do. The engine starts at the scene whose id matches `startScene`.

startScene.description: Scene id where the simulation begins.

endings.description: Possible end states, evaluated in array order against final state when a scene has no nextScene (or an explicit isFinal scene is reached). First matching condition wins.

id.description: Unique scene identifier, referenced by nextScene pointers.

domainId.description: Which domain (from top-level `domains` array) this scene belongs to. Drives the progress-rail UI.

isDetour.description: True if this scene is a branch/consequence scene rather than part of the main spine. Used for UI styling (e.g., a 'you took a wrong turn' visual treatment) and analytics.

narrative.description: Story/context text shown before the decision prompt. Supports basic markdown (bold, italics, line breaks) — render with a markdown-safe component, not raw HTML.

characterContext.description: Optional structured metadata about who is speaking/present in this scene, for richer UI (avatar, name tag, etc.). Omit if not needed.

explanation.description: Full BA-style explanation shown AFTER the candidate picks an option and sees per-option feedback — a synthesizing summary of the underlying principle being tested, written at the same depth as a standard MCQ explanation. Markdown supported.

prompt.description: The question posed to the candidate for this scene.

id.description: Letter or short code for this option.

text.description: The option text shown to the candidate.

isCorrect.description: Whether this is the best-practice answer. Used for scoring and for visual treatment (checkmark/x) after selection.

feedback.description: Immediate, short reaction shown right after this option is picked, before the longer scene-level `explanation`. Markdown supported.

stateChanges.description: Deltas applied to the simulation's numeric state when this option is chosen. Keys must match keys present in top-level `initialState`. Positive or negative integers.

setFlags.description: String flags added to a running flags[] array in state. Used later by scenes/endings for conditional narrative or branching (e.g., a scene can check 'if flags includes skipped_validation, show different opening line').

nextScene.description: Scene id to navigate to after this option is resolved. Multiple options may point to the same nextScene (convergence) or to different scenes (branching). Use the special value 'EVALUATE_ENDING' if this option ends the simulation immediately regardless of normal flow.

condition.description: Evaluated against final state. All provided keys must be satisfied (AND logic). Supported comparator suffixes: Min (>=), Max (<=), Equals.

narrative.description: Closing story text shown to the candidate.

recommendedReview.description: Domain ids the candidate should revisit, typically populated based on which domains had the most incorrect picks. Can be computed client-side from the per-scene/per-domain answer log rather than hardcoded.
